answer.line: Two OH^- per Ba(OH)2 makes [OH^-] = 0.020 M, between 0.01 and 0.1. So pOH is 1.70 and pH is 12.3.

steps: Count the hydroxide first. Each Ba(OH)2 releases two OH^-, so 0.010 M of it gives 0.020 M OH^-.
Place it on the log ruler. 0.020 is 2 x 10^-2, so pOH = 2 - log 2 = 2 - 0.30 = 1.70.
Flip to pH: 14 - 1.70 = 12.3. A strong base this concentrated belongs above pH 12.

choices.note: No one slip from 0.010 or 0.020 M lands here; pH 11 needs [OH^-] = 0.001 M. Check the decade first.
pH 12.0 comes from 0.010 M, the Ba(OH)2 itself. Each formula unit gives two OH^-, so [OH^-] is 0.020 M.
This puts pOH at 1 + 0.30 = 1.3. 0.020 sits nearer 0.01, so count down from 2: 2 - 0.30 = 1.70.
pH 13 needs [OH^-] = 0.1 M, five times this solution. 0.020 M gives pOH 1.70.

lockIt: Count every OH^- per formula unit, take pOH from [OH^-], then pH = 14 - pOH.
